name: NY-22
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 4 points on PVI
Mannion is an incumbent with a large financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs $187K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 94-95%
No public polling or expert ratings to challenge the fundamentals
model.rationale: Mannion combines a Democratic-leaning seat, incumbency, and a roughly ten-to-one cash advantage, while markets price his reelection around 94-95%. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable but not overwhelming Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late public polling or a surge of outside spending against Mannion would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent John Mannion defends a Syracuse-area seat that leans Democratic by about four points. He has raised $2.7 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican challenger Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with $187,000 available and no reported outside spending on either side. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price a Democratic win at roughly 94-95 percent. The combination of a favorable district, incumbency, and a decisive money edge points to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
